items.about: Toronto-TMC: Healthy Planet is restoring the heritage facade of 509 Parliament Street. All work will be done from a scaffold against the building face, inside a 1.22 m (4'-0") work zone along the 23.3 m frontage. The work zone is enclosed, and all equipment and materials stay inside it. No live travel lanes will be closed. The occupation is limited to the sidewalk and the northbound curb parking lane directly in front of the building. The northbound travel lane and both southbound lanes stay open at full width. Pedestrians stay on the same side of the street on an open walkway with at least 1.8 m clear. The walkway extends onto a level, slip-resistant deck in the parking lane, protected by temporary concrete barrier along the building frontage only. The barrier segment opposite the fire hydrant is removable, so Toronto Fire Services keep access.

Multiplex Construction Canada will be managing the construction of the New Etobicoke Civic Centre Located at 3755 Bloor Street W. Etobicoke, Ontario M9A 1A2, located within the newly redeveloped Etobicoke Civic Centre Precinct (formerly the Westwood Theatre Lands). The ECC is a mixed-use building comprising a wide range of community focused program and services. The building is arranged in a series of tall volumes towards the north, housing the municipal offices, while the lower floors towards the south contain all the public functions. It will also be compliant to the Toronto Accessibility Design Guidelines (TADG) to extend greater accessibility for all users. items.where: Harbour St 48 m East of Lake Shore Blvd W to 48 m East of Lake Shore Blvd W
items.about: Toronto-TMC: https://qtower.ca/ The development site is approximately 0.5 hectares in size located on the east side of Lower Simcoe Street, the south side of Harbour Street, and is bounded to the east and south by the Waterclub Condominiums (8 York Street, 208, and 218 Queens Quay West). In completion, the building will be a 59-storey mixed-use building with a total of 984 units. The building is served by a 4-storey underground parking garage that accommodates both residential and commercial parking. Parking, drop-off and loading is internal to the site and accessed from Harbour Street. Additionally, the development includes the dedication of an on-site public park and public realm improvements with more generous sidewalks, landscaping and dedicated cyclists infrastructure. The development is subject to site-specific By-law 1012-2022 and received NOAC on March 11, 2025. Through the Site Plan process, a Construction Management Plan dated February 20, 2024, prepared by Rockwell Tor
